Senses.Explanation: Far from the sages in time — the corpus's standing diagnosis of a thin age, first sighed over Danxia and then turned against itself: no last phase of the way, no excuse at the eye's falling. The origin. Nanyang Huizhong, national teacher: Danxia comes to visit and has barely spread his mat when the teacher says — no need, no need. Danxia steps back three paces. Thus it is, thus it is. He steps forward three paces. It is not so, it is not so. Danxia circles the seat once and walks out. Says the teacher: far from the sages in time, men are mostly slack — thirty years on, to find even one man will be hard. Baofu's comment: Danxia hurried his journey and never felt his weariness. Foyan Qingyuan refuses the excuse the clause had become: nowadays, far from the sages in time, men are slack — the usual talk runs true phase, semblance phase, last phase. Says this mountain monk: the way has no true, semblance, or last phase — the way of the buddha is always in the world. Hit the moment and it is the true phase; miss the moment and it is semblance and last. You must resolve to settle this thing; the crux is getting out of birth-and-death — and birth-and-death was never there to get out of: seek it in the three times and it cannot be found. The past buddhas said it — the past mind cannot be got, the present mind cannot be got, the future mind cannot be got. Then who is the one, distinct upon distinct, listening to the way right now? And Gaofeng Yuanmiao, over the litany of the old hard years: ah — in the last phase, far from the sages in time, there is a whole breed of drifting types who simply do not believe there is a gate of awakening; they only bore on this side and reckon on that side. Grant the reckoning done and the boring finished — when the eyes fall to the ground, will any of it serve? If it would serve, why did the World-Honored One need six years in the snow mountains, Bodhidharma nine years at Shaolin, Changqing seven mats worn through sitting, Xianglin forty years to make one piece, Zhaozhou thirty years with no mixed intentions — why did they buy themselves all that suffering? Zhongfeng Mingben turns the clause into the reason the institutions exist: the earlier ones knew full well the direct pointing of no-letters-established — but because far from the sages in time, men's hearts sink day by day, their will to embody the way no longer close-grained, their consciousness chasing objects daily adrift — they had no choice but to rescue it. Before Baizhang built the monasteries, men went ragged and unwashed, lingering in empty mountains and great marshes, all-out for the way; by Baizhang's time there were already the old, the sick, the fearful — hence the monastery compound, to comfort the old and sick and support the way of the patriarchs. Had the elders not bent to the times and deftly set up the means, the two words direct-pointing would long since have died out unheard. Guting Shanjian, writing to the old pine monk: grieved for the grove's autumn season — far from the sages in time, everyone scrambling for snail-horn profit and fame, nursing hawk-stinking curds, not working on what is real, drumming up hollow heads; where they open their mouths, mostly book-drilling; when a thought rises, all dust-world opinions. Pile flowers and cluster brocade as they may, matching four-six into essays and pairing four-five into lines, holding mere mind-objects all the while — the true cause is lost entire; even should the root-light stir, they take the thief for their son. And Kongyin Daodu, writing to the scholar Huang: for the beginner the work is truly hard — no road ahead, the old dwelling lost behind, nothing to stand the foot on; none but the great-rooted fail to fall back. Add to it that far from the sages in time the demons are strong and the way weak: the few who incline to this gate take blessing-making and good works for the ultimate, flatly refusing to believe there is a truth of seeing the nature and attaining the way on the spot — one who hears mind-itself-is-buddha and does not turn his head is truly hard to find. Your wisdom outruns most — encourage yourself: the great matter of birth-and-death, the swiftness of impermanence — do not just chant it past as a line. Baiyu Jingsi, at the installation on Mount Shanqing: of late, far from the sages in time, the demons are strong and the way weak — Shanqing has come to this pass with no way out of it: he can only strip off the robe of jewels and don the tattered cloth, reach his hand into the market dust, drag through water and mud, hoping to find one man, or even half of one, to repay the buddha's kindness above and bring beings across below, set on keeping the true way circulating. And just at such a moment, how to celebrate? Two wheels, sun and moon, brighten the sage virtue; a hundred million mountains and rivers swell the royal design.
